docs.title: go-atlassian
docs.text:
go-atlassian is a Go SDK and CLI for Jira that provides:

  • REST API client (rest/) - wrapper around go-jira with additional utilities
  • XML parser (xml/) - parse Jira XML exports when API access is unavailable
  • JQL builder (root package) - programmatically construct JQL queries
  • CLI tool (cmd/gojira/) - command-line interface optimized for AI agents and humans

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Multiple output formats: JSON, Table, and TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation)
  • Flexible authentication: Environment variables, goauth credential files, or CLI flags
  • AI-agent friendly: Non-interactive mode, structured output, consistent exit codes
  • Lightweight core: Root package has no external dependencies

docs.title: Package Structure
docs.text: Package Description Dependencies root JQL builder, config, constants None (lightweight) gojira/rest REST API client go-jira SDK go-atlassian/xml XML export parser None go-atlassian/web URL helpers None

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
CLISDK 
# Search issues
gojira search --jql "project = FOO AND status = Open"

# Get issue details
gojira get ISSUE-123

# Show statistics
gojira stats --jql "project = FOO" --by status --format table

import "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"

client, err := jira.NewClientFromBasicAuth(
    "https://your-instance.atlassian.net",
    "your-email@example.com",
    "your-api-token",
    false,
)

issues, err := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssues("project = FOO", false)

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
1. Automate Jira operations - Search, update, and export issues via CLI
  2. Build custom integrations - Use the SDK to integrate Jira with other systems
  3. Generate reports - Export issues to JSON/XLSX for analysis
  4. AI agent workflows - Token-optimized output for LLM consumption
  5. Parse XML exports - Access Jira data when API is unavailable

docs.title: CLI Installation
docs.text:
Install the gojira command-line tool:

go install github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/cmd/gojira@latest

Verify the installation:

gojira version

docs.title: SDK Installation
docs.text:
Add go-atlassian as a dependency to your Go project:

go get github.com/grokify/go-atlassian

Import the packages you need:

import (
    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian"       // JQL builder, config
    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"  // REST API client
    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/xml"   // XML parser
)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Go 1.21 or later
  • Jira Cloud or Jira Server instance
  • API token (for Jira Cloud) or username/password (for Jira Server)

docs.title: Getting an API Token
docs.text:
For Jira Cloud, you need an API token instead of your password:

  1. Go to Atlassian API Tokens
  2. Click Create API token
  3. Give it a descriptive name (e.g., "gojira CLI")
  4. Copy the token - you won't see it again

Keep your token secure

API tokens provide full access to your Jira account. Never commit them to version control or share them publicly.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get up and running with go-atlassian in minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go 1.21 or later installed
  • Access to a Jira instance (Cloud or Server)
  • API token or credentials

docs.title: 1. Install the CLI
docs.text: go install github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/cmd/gojira@latest

docs.title: 2. Configure Authentication
docs.text:
Set environment variables for your Jira instance:

export JIRA_URL=https://your-instance.atlassian.net
export JIRA_USER=your-email@example.com
export JIRA_TOKEN=your-api-token

Add to your shell profile

Add these exports to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc to persist them.

docs.title: 3. Search for Issues
docs.text:
# Search for open issues in a project
gojira search --jql "project = FOO AND status = Open"

# Get the first 10 results
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --max 10

# Output as human-readable table
gojira search --jql "assignee = currentUser()" --table

docs.title: 4. Get Issue Details
docs.text:
# Get a single issue
gojira get ISSUE-123

# Get multiple issues
gojira get ISSUE-123 ISSUE-456

# Include changelog
gojira get ISSUE-123 --expand

docs.title: 5. View Statistics
docs.text:
# Count issues by status
gojira stats --jql "project = FOO" --by status --format table

# Count by assignee
gojira stats --jql "project = FOO" --by assignee

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
go-atlassian supports three output formats:

Format Flag Use Case JSON --json Default, machine-readable Table --table Human-readable TOON --toon Token-optimized for LLMs

Example:

# JSON output (default)
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --json

# Table output
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --table

# TOON output (efficient for AI agents)
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --toon

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: The gojira command-line interface provides commands for searching, retrieving, and managing Jira issues.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go install github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/cmd/gojira@latest

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Description search Search issues with JQL get Get one or more issues by key comments Get comments for an issue patch Update issue fields export Export issues to JSON or XLSX fields List and filter custom fields stats Show issue statistics grouped by field version Show version information

docs.title: Global Flags
docs.text:
These flags are available on all commands:

Flag Short Description --json -j Output as JSON (default) --table -t Output as human-readable table --toon Output as TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation) --creds-file Path to goauth credentials file --account Account key in credentials file --quiet -q Suppress non-essential output

docs.title: JSON (default)
docs.text:
Machine-readable JSON output, ideal for piping to jq or programmatic processing:

gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --json | jq '.[].key'

docs.title: Table
docs.text:
Human-readable ASCII table:

gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --table

Output:

KEY        TYPE    STATUS    SUMMARY
FOO-123    Bug     Open      Fix login issue
FOO-124    Story   Done      Add user profile

docs.title: TOON
docs.text:
Token-Optimized Object Notation - compact format optimized for LLM consumption:

gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --toon

TOON format uses abbreviated keys and is approximately 8x more token-efficient than JSON.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The CLI authenticates in this order:

  1. CLI flags: --creds-file and --account
  2. Environment variables: JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, JIRA_TOKEN
  3. goauth file: ~/.config/goauth/credentials.json

See Authentication for details.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Error (authentication failure, API error, invalid arguments)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Search with environment variables
export JIRA_URL=https://your-instance.atlassian.net
export JIRA_USER=your-email@example.com
export JIRA_TOKEN=your-api-token
gojira search --jql "project = FOO"

# Search with credentials file
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --creds-file ~/.config/goauth/creds.json --account myaccount

# Quiet mode (suppress progress messages)
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" -q

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: go-atlassian supports multiple authentication methods to connect to your Jira instance.

docs.title: Authentication Priority
docs.text:
The CLI checks authentication sources in this order:

  1. CLI flags (--creds-file, --account)
  2. Environment variables (JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, JIRA_TOKEN)
  3. goauth credentials file (~/.config/goauth/credentials.json)

docs.title: Method 1: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Set these environment variables:

export JIRA_URL=https://your-instance.atlassian.net
export JIRA_USER=your-email@example.com
export JIRA_TOKEN=your-api-token

This is the recommended method for:

  • Local development
  • CI/CD pipelines
  • Docker containers
  • AI agent integrations

Non-interactive

Environment variables enable fully non-interactive operation, ideal for automation.

docs.title: Method 2: goauth Credentials File
docs.text: go-atlassian integrates with goauth for credential management.

docs.title: Default Location
docs.text: ~/.config/goauth/credentials.json

docs.title: File Format
docs.text:
{
  "credentials": {
    "jira-prod": {
      "service": "jira",
      "type": "basic",
      "basic": {
        "serverURL": "https://your-instance.atlassian.net",
        "username": "your-email@example.com",
        "password": "your-api-token"
      }
    },
    "jira-staging": {
      "service": "jira",
      "type": "basic",
      "basic": {
        "serverURL": "https://staging.atlassian.net",
        "username": "your-email@example.com",
        "password": "your-staging-token"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Using a Specific Account
docs.text:
# Use account key from default credentials file
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --account jira-prod

# Use custom credentials file
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --creds-file ~/my-creds.json --account myaccount

docs.title: Interactive Selection
docs.text: If no --account is specified, goauth will interactively prompt you to select an account.

docs.title: Jira Cloud
docs.text:
1. Go to Atlassian API Tokens
  2. Click Create API token
  3. Give it a descriptive name (e.g., "gojira CLI")
  4. Copy the token immediately

docs.title: Jira Server / Data Center
docs.text: Use your Jira password or create a personal access token in your Jira Server settings.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
Keep credentials secure

  • Never commit credentials to version control
  • Use environment variables in CI/CD
  • Restrict API token permissions when possible
  • Rotate tokens periodically

docs.title: Using .envrc with direnv
docs.text:
For project-specific credentials, use direnv:

# .envrc (add to .gitignore)
export JIRA_URL=https://your-instance.atlassian.net
export JIRA_USER=your-email@example.com
export JIRA_TOKEN=your-api-token

Then run:

direnv allow

docs.title: "authentication failed" Error
docs.text:
1. Verify your credentials are correct
  2. Check that JIRA_URL includes https://
  3. Ensure your API token hasn't expired
  4. Verify you have access to the Jira project

docs.title: Testing Authentication
docs.text:
# Test with a simple query
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --max 1

# Check version (no auth required)
gojira version

docs.title: comments
docs.text: Get comments for a Jira issue.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: gojira comments <issue-key> [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description issue-key The Jira issue key (e.g., FOO-123)

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --max 50 Maximum number of comments to return

Plus global flags.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Get comments for an issue
gojira comments FOO-123

# Limit to 10 most recent comments
gojira comments FOO-123 --max 10

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
# Get comment count
gojira comments FOO-123 -q | jq '.total'

# Get latest comment body
gojira comments FOO-123 --max 1 -q | jq -r '.comments[0].body'

# List all comment authors
gojira comments FOO-123 -q | jq -r '.comments[].author'

docs.title: JSON Format
docs.text:
{
  "key": "FOO-123",
  "total": 3,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": "10001",
      "author": "John Doe",
      "body": "I've started working on this issue.",
      "created": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000+0000",
      "updated": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000+0000"
    },
    {
      "id": "10002",
      "author": "Jane Smith",
      "body": "Please check the latest commit.",
      "created": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000+0000",
      "updated": "2024-01-16T14:25:00.000+0000"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Review Discussion History
docs.text:
# Get full comment thread for context
gojira comments FOO-123

docs.title: AI Agent Workflows
docs.text:
# Get recent discussion for LLM context
gojira comments FOO-123 --max 5 -q

docs.title: Integration with Other Tools
docs.text:
# Export comments to a file
gojira comments FOO-123 > comments.json

# Combine with issue details
echo '{"issue":' && gojira get FOO-123 -q && echo ',"comments":' && gojira comments FOO-123 -q && echo '}'

docs.title: create
docs.text: Create a Jira issue from a YAML file.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: gojira create -f <file> [flags]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Short Description --file -f YAML file containing issue data (required) --dry-run Validate and preview without creating --project Override project key from file --parent Override parent issue key from file --type Override issue type from file --json -j Output full result as JSON

docs.title: YAML Format
docs.text: The YAML file supports all standard Jira fields plus custom fields.

docs.title: Standard Fields
docs.text: Field Required Description project Yes Project key (e.g., PROJ) type Yes Issue type (Story, Bug, Task, Epic) summary Yes Issue title description No Issue description (supports Jira markdown) parent No Parent issue key for subtasks or stories under epics labels No List of labels priority No Priority name (High, Medium, Low) assignee No Username or email reporter No Username or email components No List of component names fix_versions No List of fix version names

docs.title: Custom Fields
docs.text:
Any field starting with customfield_ is passed directly to the Jira API:

customfield_12345: "Value for custom field"
customfield_10001: "Q2-2024"

docs.title: Basic Story
docs.text:
project: PROJ
type: Story
summary: Add user authentication
description: |
  Implement OAuth2 login flow for the application.
labels:
  - auth
  - mvp

gojira create -f story.yaml
# Output: Created PROJ-123

docs.title: Full Example with Custom Fields
docs.text:
project: PROJ
type: Story
summary: Add user authentication via OAuth2
description: |
  ## Background
  Users currently have no way to securely authenticate. We need to implement
  OAuth2 login flow to support SSO with corporate identity providers.

  ## Requirements
  - Support Google and Microsoft identity providers
  - Store refresh tokens securely
  - Handle token expiration gracefully

  ## Technical Notes
  Use the existing session middleware for token validation.
parent: PROJ-100
labels:
  - auth
  - mvp
  - security
priority: High
assignee: john.doe
components:
  - backend
  - security
customfield_12345: |
  Given a user is on the login page
  When they click "Sign in with Google"
  Then they should be redirected to Google OAuth
  And upon success, redirected back to the dashboard
customfield_10001: Q2-2024

docs.title: Dry Run
docs.text:
Preview what would be created without actually creating:

gojira create -f story.yaml --dry-run

Output:

{
  "valid": true,
  "project": "PROJ",
  "type": "Story",
  "summary": "Add user authentication via OAuth2",
  "description": "## Background\n...",
  "parent": "PROJ-100",
  "labels": ["auth", "mvp", "security"],
  "priority": "High",
  "assignee": "john.doe",
  "custom_fields": {
    "customfield_12345": "Given a user is on the login page..."
  }
}

docs.title: Override Project or Parent
docs.text:
# Create in a different project
gojira create -f story.yaml --project OTHER

# Create under a different epic
gojira create -f story.yaml --parent EPIC-456

# Override issue type
gojira create -f story.yaml --type Task

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
Get full response including issue ID and self URL:

gojira create -f story.yaml --json

Output:

Created PROJ-123
{
  "key": "PROJ-123",
  "id": "10001",
  "self": "https://company.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue/10001",
  "summary": "Add user authentication via OAuth2"
}

docs.title: Multiline Strings
docs.text:
Use YAML block scalars for multiline content:

Syntax Behavior \| Preserves newlines (literal) > Folds newlines to spaces 
# Literal block - preserves newlines
description: |
  Line 1
  Line 2

  Line 4 after blank

# Folded block - joins lines
description: >
  This becomes one long
  paragraph joined together.

For markdown code blocks, use the literal style (|):

description: |
  ## Example

  ```go
  func main() {
      fmt.Println("Hello")
  }
  ```

docs.title: export
docs.text: Export Jira issues to JSON or XLSX format.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: gojira export [flags]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Description --jql JQL query to search issues --keys Comma-separated issue keys to export --json Output JSON file path --xlsx Output XLSX file path --from-json Read issues from existing JSON file instead of querying --include-parents Include parent issues in export --sheet Sheet name for XLSX export (default: "issues")

Plus global flags.

docs.title: Export to JSON
docs.text:
# Export search results to JSON
gojira export --jql "project = FOO" --json issues.json

# Export specific issues
gojira export --keys FOO-1,FOO-2,FOO-3 --json output.json

docs.title: Export to Excel
docs.text:
# Export to XLSX
gojira export --jql "project = FOO AND status = Open" --xlsx report.xlsx

# Custom sheet name
gojira export --jql "project = FOO" --xlsx report.xlsx --sheet "Open Issues"

docs.title: Export Both Formats
docs.text:
# Export to both JSON and XLSX
gojira export --jql "project = FOO" --json backup.json --xlsx report.xlsx

docs.title: Include Parent Issues
docs.text:
When exporting sub-tasks or stories linked to epics, include the parent issues:

gojira export --jql "project = FOO AND issuetype = Sub-task" --include-parents --xlsx subtasks.xlsx

docs.title: Convert JSON to XLSX
docs.text:
If you have an existing JSON export, convert it to XLSX:

gojira export --from-json issues.json --xlsx report.xlsx

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
The JSON file contains the full issue data including all fields:

{
  "issues": [
    {
      "key": "FOO-123",
      "fields": {
        "summary": "Fix login bug",
        "status": {"name": "Open"},
        ...
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: XLSX Output
docs.text:
The Excel file contains a table with columns:

  • Key
  • Type
  • Status
  • Priority
  • Summary
  • Assignee
  • Created
  • Updated
  • And more...

docs.title: Backup Issues
docs.text:
# Regular backup of project issues
gojira export --jql "project = FOO" --json "backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).json"

docs.title: Generate Reports
docs.text:
# Sprint report
gojira export --jql "project = FOO AND sprint = 'Sprint 42'" --xlsx sprint-42.xlsx

# Unresolved bugs report
gojira export --jql "project = FOO AND type = Bug AND resolution is EMPTY" --xlsx bugs.xlsx

docs.title: Data Analysis
docs.text:
# Export for external analysis
gojira export --jql "project = FOO AND created >= -30d" --json recent.json

# Then use with jq, Python, etc.
cat recent.json | jq '.issues | length'

docs.title: fields
docs.text: List and filter Jira custom fields.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: gojira fields [flags]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Description --id Filter by field ID(s), comma-separated --name Filter by name (partial match) --name-exact Filter by exact name --custom-only Show only custom fields (exclude system fields) --epic-link Show Epic Link field --json Output as JSON --table Output as table (default) --project Filter by project key (shows only fields available in project) --issue-type Filter by issue type ID (requires --project) --show-duplicates Show only fields with duplicate names

Plus global flags.

docs.title: List All Fields
docs.text:
# List all custom fields as table
gojira fields

# List as JSON
gojira fields --json

docs.title: Filter by ID
docs.text:
# Get specific field
gojira fields --id customfield_10001

# Get multiple fields
gojira fields --id customfield_10001,customfield_10002

docs.title: Search by Name
docs.text:
# Partial match search
gojira fields --name "Epic"

# Exact name match
gojira fields --name-exact "Epic Link"

docs.title: Custom Fields Only
docs.text:
# Exclude system fields
gojira fields --custom-only

docs.title: Get Epic Link Field
docs.text:
Find the Epic Link field (useful for linking issues to epics):

gojira fields --epic-link

docs.title: Filter by Project
docs.text:
Show only fields available in a specific project:

# Fields available in project ABC
gojira fields --project ABC

# Fields for a specific issue type in project
gojira fields --project ABC --issue-type 10001

docs.title: Find Duplicate Field Names
docs.text:
Identify fields that share the same display name (common when copying schemes or reinstalling apps):

# Show only fields with duplicate names
gojira fields --show-duplicates

This helps identify ambiguous field names that may cause issues when querying by name.

docs.title: Table Format
docs.text:
ID                  NAME              TYPE         CUSTOM
customfield_10001   Epic Link         string       true
customfield_10002   Story Points      number       true
customfield_10003   Sprint            array        true

docs.title: JSON Format
docs.text:
[
  {
    "id": "customfield_10001",
    "name": "Epic Link",
    "custom": true,
    "schema": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Find Field IDs for Queries
docs.text:
# Find the Sprint field ID
gojira fields --name Sprint

# Use in search
gojira search --jql "project = FOO AND cf[10003] is not EMPTY"

docs.title: Discover Available Fields
docs.text:
# See all custom fields your Jira has
gojira fields --custom-only | head -20

docs.title: Script Integration
docs.text:
# Get Epic Link field ID
EPIC_FIELD=$(gojira fields --epic-link --json | jq -r '.[0].id')
echo "Epic Link field: $EPIC_FIELD"

docs.title: get
docs.text: Get one or more Jira issues by their keys.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: gojira get <issue-key> [issue-key...] [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description issue-key One or more Jira issue keys (e.g., FOO-123)

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --expand false Expand changelog and other fields --fields Comma-separated list of fields to include --raw false Output full API JSON instead of simplified metadata

Plus global flags.

docs.title: Single Issue
docs.text:
# Get a single issue
gojira get FOO-123

# Human-readable output
gojira get FOO-123 --table

docs.title: Multiple Issues
docs.text:
# Get multiple issues
gojira get FOO-123 FOO-456 FOO-789

# Output as JSON array
gojira get FOO-123 FOO-456 --json

docs.title: With Changelog
docs.text:
# Include issue history
gojira get FOO-123 --expand

docs.title: Full API JSON
docs.text:
# Output complete API response (all fields)
gojira get FOO-123 --raw

The --raw flag outputs the full jira.Issue JSON from the API instead of the simplified metadata format. Use this when you need access to all fields including custom fields, comments, or other data not included in the default output.

docs.title: JSON Format (Default)
docs.text:
The default output is a simplified metadata format:

[
  {
    "key": "FOO-123",
    "type": "Bug",
    "status": "Open",
    "summary": "Fix login bug",
    "description": "Users cannot log in when...",
    "project": "Foo Project",
    "projectKey": "FOO",
    "assignee": "John Doe",
    "creator": "Jane Smith",
    "created": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "updated": "2024-01-16T14:20:00Z",
    "labels": ["urgent", "backend"]
  }
]

docs.title: Raw JSON Format (--raw)
docs.text:
The --raw flag outputs the complete API response:

[
  {
    "key": "FOO-123",
    "fields": {
      "summary": "Fix login bug",
      "description": "Users cannot log in when...",
      "status": { "name": "Open" },
      "issuetype": { "name": "Bug" },
      "priority": { "name": "High" },
      "assignee": { "displayName": "John Doe" },
      "created": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000+0000",
      "updated": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000+0000"
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Table Format
docs.text:
KEY        TYPE    STATUS    PRIORITY    ASSIGNEE     SUMMARY
FOO-123    Bug     Open      High        John Doe     Fix login bug

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
# Get issue and extract status
STATUS=$(gojira get FOO-123 -q | jq -r '.[0].fields.status.name')
echo "Issue status: $STATUS"

# Check if issue is closed
if [[ $(gojira get FOO-123 -q | jq -r '.[0].fields.status.name') == "Closed" ]]; then
  echo "Issue is closed"
fi

docs.title: AI Agent Workflows
docs.text:
# Get issue details for LLM context
gojira get FOO-123 --toon

docs.title: patch
docs.text: Update one or more fields on a Jira issue.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: gojira patch <issue-key> [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description issue-key The Jira issue key to update (e.g., FOO-123)

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Description --set Set field value (format: field=value). Can be repeated. --add-label Add a label to the issue. Can be repeated. --remove-label Remove a label from the issue. Can be repeated. --json Raw JSON body for complex updates --dry-run Show request body without executing --show-after Show issue after update

Plus global flags.

gojira patch FOO-123 --set summary="New summary"

docs.title: AI Agents Guide
docs.text: go-atlassian is designed to work well with AI agents like Claude Code. This guide covers best practices for AI-agent workflows.

docs.title: Why go-atlassian for AI Agents?
docs.text:
1. Non-interactive operation: All auth via environment variables or files
  2. Structured output: JSON and TOON formats for reliable parsing
  3. Consistent exit codes: 0 for success, 1 for errors
  4. Token efficiency: TOON format reduces token consumption by ~8x
  5. Quiet mode: Suppress progress messages for cleaner output

docs.title: TOON Format
docs.text:
TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation) is a compact format designed for LLM consumption:

# JSON output (verbose)
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --json

# TOON output (compact)
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --toon

docs.title: TOON Example
docs.text:
JSON: 

{
  "field": "status",
  "total": 150,
  "results": [
    {"value": "Done", "count": 75},
    {"value": "Open", "count": 45}
  ]
}

TOON: 

f:status|t:150|r:[{v:Done,n:75},{v:Open,n:45}]

The TOON format uses abbreviated keys (f for field, t for total, etc.) and minimal punctuation.

docs.title: Environment Setup
docs.text:
Set credentials via environment variables for non-interactive operation:

export JIRA_URL=https://your-instance.atlassian.net
export JIRA_USER=your-email@example.com
export JIRA_TOKEN=your-api-token

docs.title: 1. Search and Parse Issues
docs.text:
# Search for issues (quiet mode, TOON output)
gojira search --jql "project = FOO AND status = Open" --toon -q

# Search with JSON for detailed parsing
gojira search --jql "project = FOO" --json -q | jq '.[].key'

docs.title: 2. Get Issue Details
docs.text:
# Get single issue
gojira get FOO-123 --toon -q

# Get multiple issues
gojira get FOO-123 FOO-456 --json -q

docs.title: 3. Analyze Issue Distribution
docs.text:
# Status breakdown
gojira stats --jql "project = FOO" --by status --format json -q

# Type breakdown
gojira stats --jql "project = FOO" --by type --format json -q

docs.title: 4. Update Issues
docs.text:
# Add label
gojira patch FOO-123 --add-label reviewed -q

# Set field
gojira patch FOO-123 --set priority=High -q

docs.title: 5. Export for Analysis
docs.text:
# Export to JSON
gojira export --jql "project = FOO" --json issues.json -q

# Export to XLSX
gojira export --jql "project = FOO" --xlsx report.xlsx -q

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Check exit codes for automation:

if gojira search --jql "project = FOO" -q > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Search succeeded"
else
    echo "Search failed"
fi

docs.title: Token Optimization Tips
docs.text:
1. Use TOON format: --toon uses ~8x fewer tokens than JSON
  2. Use quiet mode: -q suppresses progress messages
  3. Limit results: --max 10 for quick checks
  4. Use stats: Get summaries instead of raw issues

docs.title: Example: Efficient Sprint Status Check
docs.text:
# Inefficient (returns full issue data)
gojira search --jql "sprint = 'Sprint 42'" --json

# Efficient (returns summary counts)
gojira stats --jql "sprint = 'Sprint 42'" --by status --format toon -q

docs.title: SDK Integration
docs.text:
For programmatic AI agent integration:

package main

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "os"

    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"
)

func main() {
    // Create client from environment
    client, err := jira.NewClientFromBasicAuth(
        os.Getenv("JIRA_URL"),
        os.Getenv("JIRA_USER"),
        os.Getenv("JIRA_TOKEN"),
        false,
    )
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: %v\n", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }

    // Search and output JSON
    issues, err := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssues("project = FOO", false)
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: %v\n", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }

    // Output as JSON for LLM parsing
    data, _ := json.Marshal(issues)
    fmt.Println(string(data))
}

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
1. Use environment variables for credentials, not CLI flags
  2. Use goauth files with appropriate file permissions
  3. Never log credentials in AI agent outputs
  4. Limit API token scope when possible

docs.title: Working with Custom Fields
docs.text: Custom fields are user-defined fields in Jira that extend the default issue schema. This guide covers how to discover, use, and manage custom fields with go-atlassian.

docs.title: Understanding Custom Field IDs
docs.text:
Every custom field in Jira has a unique ID in the format customfield_NNNNN (e.g., customfield_10001). While Jira displays friendly names like "Story Points" or "Epic Link", the API uses these IDs internally.

Important: Multiple fields can share the same display name (e.g., after copying project schemes). Always verify field IDs when working with custom fields.

docs.title: List All Custom Fields
docs.text:
# List all custom fields
gojira fields

# Output as JSON for programmatic use
gojira fields --json

docs.title: Filter by Project
docs.text:
# Fields available in a specific project
gojira fields --project PROJ

# Fields for a specific issue type in a project
gojira fields --project PROJ --issue-type Story

docs.title: Find Required Fields
docs.text:
# Show only required fields for issue creation
gojira fields --project PROJ --issue-type Bug --required

docs.title: Identify Duplicate Names
docs.text:
# Find fields with duplicate names
gojira fields --duplicates

docs.title: Using Custom Fields in JQL
docs.text:
Custom fields in JQL can be referenced by:

  1. Clause name (if defined): "Epic Link" = PROJ-100
  2. Field ID: cf[10001] = "value"
# Search by Epic Link
gojira search "'Epic Link' = PROJ-100"

# Search by Sprint
gojira search "Sprint = 'Sprint 5'"

# Search by Story Points range
gojira search "'Story Points' >= 5 AND 'Story Points' <= 13"

docs.title: YAML Format
docs.text:
When creating issues, use the exact field ID in your YAML file:

project: PROJ
type: Story
summary: Add user authentication
description: |
  Implement OAuth2 login flow.

# Custom fields use their IDs
customfield_10001: 8              # Story Points
customfield_10002: PROJ-100       # Epic Link
customfield_10003:                # Sprint (array type)
  - name: "Sprint 5"
customfield_10004: "High"         # Priority dropdown
customfield_10005:                # Multi-select
  - value: "Option A"
  - value: "Option B"

docs.title: Validate Before Creating
docs.text:
Use --validate to check your custom fields against the Jira API:

gojira create -f story.yaml --validate

This will report:

  • Missing required fields
  • Unknown field IDs
  • Available fields for the issue type

docs.title: Field Type Formats
docs.text:
Different custom field types require different value formats:

Type Format Example Text String "Simple text" Number Number 8 or 3.5 Select String "Option Name" Multi-select Array [{value: "A"}, {value: "B"}] User Object {name: "username"} Cascading Select Object {value: "Parent", child: {value: "Child"}} Date String "2024-01-15" DateTime String "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000+0000"

docs.title: Get Custom Fields
docs.text:
import "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"

// Get all custom fields
fields, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFields()
if err != nil {
    return err
}

// Filter by name
epicLinkFields := fields.FilterByNames("Epic Link")

// Get by exact ID
field, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFieldByID("customfield_10001")

docs.title: Find Fields with Suggestions
docs.text:
// When a field name doesn't match exactly, get suggestions
field, suggestions := fields.FindByNameWithSuggestions("Sprnt")
if field == nil {
    fmt.Println("Did you mean:")
    for _, s := range suggestions {
        fmt.Printf("  - %s (%s)\n", s.Name, s.ID)
    }
}

docs.title: Get Project-Specific Fields
docs.text:
ctx := context.Background()

// Get fields available in a specific project
projectFields, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFieldsForProject(ctx, "PROJ")
if err != nil {
    return err
}

// Get required fields for an issue type
requiredFields, err := client.CreateMetaAPI.GetRequiredFields(ctx, "PROJ", "10001")

docs.title: Map Names to IDs
docs.text:
// Handle duplicate field names
nameToIDs := fields.MapNameToIDs()
// nameToIDs["Sprint"] might return ["customfield_10001", "customfield_10004"]

// Find duplicates
duplicates := fields.DuplicateNames()
// ["Sprint", "Module"] - fields with multiple IDs

docs.title: 1. Use Field IDs, Not Names
docs.text:
Field names can change or have duplicates. Always use IDs in automation:

# Good - stable
customfield_10001: 8

# Risky - could break if renamed or duplicated
# "Story Points": 8

docs.title: 2. Validate Field Availability
docs.text:
Fields vary by project and issue type. Always check availability:

# Before creating a Bug in PROJ
gojira fields --project PROJ --issue-type Bug

docs.title: 3. Handle Duplicates Gracefully
docs.text:
# Check for duplicates before automation
gojira fields --duplicates

# If duplicates exist, use IDs explicitly

docs.title: 4. Cache Field Metadata
docs.text:
In SDK code, create the client with custom field caching:

// Load custom fields once during client creation
client, err := jira.NewClientFromBasicAuth(url, user, token, true)
// client.CustomFieldSet is now populated

docs.title: 5. Document Your Field Mappings
docs.text:
Create a reference document mapping field names to IDs for your team:

Display Name Field ID Type Required Story Points customfield_10001 Number No Epic Link customfield_10002 Issue Link No Sprint customfield_10003 Sprint No

docs.title: "Field not found" Error
docs.text:
The field might not be available for the issue type or project:

# Check available fields
gojira fields --project PROJ --issue-type Story

docs.title: Multiple Fields with Same Name
docs.text:
Use the field ID instead of the name:

# Find the correct ID
gojira fields | grep -i "sprint"
# Use the ID in your YAML

docs.title: Wrong Value Format
docs.text: Check the field type and format your value accordingly. Use --validate to catch errors before creating issues.

Use the SDK's JQL builder for programmatic query construction:

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: Common issues and solutions when using go-atlassian.

docs.title: Error: "authentication failed"
docs.text:
Cause: Invalid credentials or missing environment variables.

Solutions:

  1. Verify environment variables are set:
echo $JIRA_URL $JIRA_USER $JIRA_TOKEN
  1. Check credentials are correct:
# Test with curl
curl -u "user@example.com:api-token" \
  "https://company.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/myself"

  1. For Jira Cloud, ensure you're using an API token (not password):

  2. Generate at: https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens

docs.title: Error: "401 Unauthorized"
docs.text:
Cause: API token expired or revoked.

Solution: Generate a new API token and update your credentials.

docs.title: Error: "403 Forbidden"
docs.text:
Cause: Insufficient permissions for the operation.

Solutions:

  1. Check your Jira permissions for the project
  2. Verify the API token has the required scopes
  3. Contact your Jira administrator

docs.title: Error: "issue not found" for valid issue key
docs.text:
Causes:

  • Issue was deleted or moved
  • No permission to view the issue
  • Wrong Jira instance

Solutions:

  1. Verify the issue exists in the Jira web UI
  2. Check you're connected to the correct Jira instance
  3. Verify your permissions on the project

docs.title: Error: "field not found" when creating issues
docs.text:
Cause: Custom field name doesn't match or field isn't available for the issue type.

Solutions:

  1. List available fields for your project:
gojira fields --project PROJ --issue-type Story
  1. Use --validate to check before creating:
gojira create -f issue.yaml --validate
  1. Use field ID instead of name:
customfield_10001: value

docs.title: Error: "multiple custom fields found with name"
docs.text:
Cause: Duplicate field names in Jira (common after copying schemes).

Solutions:

  1. Use field ID instead of name:
gojira fields --project PROJ
# Find the correct ID, then use it in your YAML
  1. Check for duplicate fields:
gojira fields --duplicates

docs.title: Error: "JQL parse error"
docs.text:
Cause: Invalid JQL syntax.

Common mistakes:

# Wrong: unquoted project name with spaces
gojira search "project = My Project"

# Correct: quote values with spaces
gojira search "project = 'My Project'"

# Wrong: invalid operator
gojira search "status <> Done"

# Correct: use != for not equal
gojira search "status != Done"

docs.title: Error: "field does not exist"
docs.text:
Cause: Using a field name that Jira doesn't recognize.

Solutions:

  1. Check field names in Jira UI
  2. Use clause names from gojira fields:
gojira fields | grep -i sprint
  1. Custom fields may need quotes:
gojira search "'Epic Link' = PROJ-100"

docs.title: Slow search queries
docs.text:
Causes:

  • Unbounded queries returning too many results
  • Complex JQL with multiple OR conditions

Solutions:

  1. Add filters to reduce results:
# Add project filter
gojira search "assignee = currentUser()" --project PROJ

# Add date filter
gojira search "project = PROJ AND updated >= -7d"
  1. Use --max to limit results:
gojira search "project = PROJ" --max 100

docs.title: Timeout errors
docs.text:
Cause: Large result sets or slow Jira server.

Solutions:

  1. Add more specific filters to reduce results
  2. Use pagination:
gojira search "project = PROJ" --max 50

docs.title: Finding the correct custom field ID
docs.text:
# List all custom fields
gojira fields

# Filter by project
gojira fields --project PROJ

# Search for specific field
gojira fields | grep -i "epic"

docs.title: Custom field not appearing in results
docs.text:
Cause: Field not in the default fields list.

Solution: Specify the field in your JQL or use --expand:

gojira get PROJ-123 --expand fields

docs.title: Error: "missing required environment variables"
docs.text:
Cause: MCP server not configured with Jira credentials.

Solution: Set all required environment variables in your MCP config:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jira": {
      "command": "gojira-mcp",
      "env": {
        "JIRA_BASE_URL": "https://company.atlassian.net",
        "JIRA_USERNAME": "user@example.com",
        "JIRA_API_TOKEN": "your-api-token"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: MCP server not responding
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Test the server manually:
echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}' | gojira-mcp

  1. Check logs (stderr) for errors

  2. Verify the binary is in your PATH:

which gojira-mcp

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
If you're still experiencing issues:

  1. Enable debug logging:
export GOJIRA_LOG_LEVEL=debug
gojira search "project = PROJ"

  1. Check the GitHub Issues

  2. Open a new issue with:

  3. gojira version (gojira version)

  4. Command that failed
  5. Full error message
  6. Relevant environment info

docs.title: Issue Transitions
docs.text:
Automate workflow transitions with the new transitions API.

import "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"

// Get available transitions for an issue
transitions, err := client.IssueAPI.GetTransitions(ctx, "ISSUE-123")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Print available transitions
for _, t := range transitions {
    fmt.Printf("ID: %s, Name: %s\n", t.ID, t.Name)
}

// Execute a transition by name
err = client.IssueAPI.DoTransitionWithNameAndPayload(ctx, "ISSUE-123", "Done", nil)

// Batch transitions
options := jira.TransitionOptionSet{
    Options: []jira.TransitionOption{
        {IssueKey: "ISSUE-1", TransitionName: "In Progress"},
        {IssueKey: "ISSUE-2", TransitionName: "Done"},
    },
}
results, err := client.IssueAPI.DoTransitions(ctx, options)

docs.title: Status Category Filtering
docs.text:
Filter and analyze issues by Jira's built-in status categories (To Do, In Progress, Done).

// Filter by status category
doneIssues := issuesSet.FilterByStatusCategory("Done")
inProgressIssues := issuesSet.FilterByStatusCategory("In Progress")

// Histogram by status category
histogram := issuesSet.HistogramByStatusCategory()
for category, count := range histogram {
    fmt.Printf("%s: %d\n", category, count)
}

// Get statuses for specific categories
categories := jira.StatusCategories{...}
statuses := categories.StatusesForCategories([]string{"Done", "In Progress"})

docs.title: Batch Issue Operations
docs.text:
Update multiple issues efficiently.

// Batch patch issues
keys := []string{"ISSUE-1", "ISSUE-2", "ISSUE-3"}
reqBody := jira.IssuePatchRequestBody{
    Fields: map[string]jira.IssuePatchRequestBodyField{
        "priority": {Value: "High"},
    },
}
results, err := client.IssueAPI.IssuesPatch(ctx, keys, reqBody)

// Batch add label
results, err := client.IssueAPI.IssuesPatchAddLabel(ctx, keys, "reviewed")

docs.title: Cached Issue Search
docs.text:
Cache search results to a file for repeated queries.

issuesSet, err := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssuesSetWithFileCache(
    "project = FOO",
    "cache/foo-issues.json",
    24*time.Hour, // Cache TTL
)

docs.title: JQL Text Search
docs.text:
New JQL builder fields for text searching.

jql := jira.JQL{
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO"}},
    SummaryLike:  []string{"login", "auth"},     // summary ~ "login" AND summary ~ "auth"
    TextLike:     []string{"error"},              // text ~ "error"
    TextNotLike:  []string{"test"},               // text !~ "test"
}

docs.text:
Calculate time from creation to resolution.

im := jira.NewIssueMore(issue)
resolutionTime := im.ResolutionTime()
if resolutionTime > 0 {
    fmt.Printf("Resolved in: %s\n", resolutionTime)
}

docs.text:

histogram, err := issuesSet.HistogramByCustomField("customfield_10001")
for value, count := range histogram {
    fmt.Printf("%s: %d\n", value, count)
}

docs.title: Example: Workflow Automation
docs.text:
Complete example automating issue transitions based on labels:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"
)

func main() {
    client, err := jira.NewClientFromBasicAuth(
        "https://your-instance.atlassian.net",
        "your-email@example.com",
        "your-api-token",
        false,
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    ctx := context.Background()

    // Find issues with "ready-for-review" label
    issues, err := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssues(
        "project = FOO AND labels = ready-for-review AND status = 'In Progress'",
        true,
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Transition each to "In Review"
    for _, issue := range issues {
        err := client.IssueAPI.DoTransitionWithNameAndPayload(ctx, issue.Key, "In Review", nil)
        if err != nil {
            log.Printf("Failed to transition %s: %v", issue.Key, err)
            continue
        }
        fmt.Printf("Transitioned %s to In Review\n", issue.Key)
    }
}

fields, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFieldsByName("Module")

// Get field by exact ID
field, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFieldByID("customfield_12345")

// Find duplicate field names
dupes := fields.DuplicateNames() // ["Module", "Sprint"]

// Map names to IDs
nameToIDs := fields.MapNameToIDs() // {"Module": ["customfield_123", "customfield_456"]}

CLI - Detect duplicates:

# Show only fields with duplicate names
gojira fields --show-duplicates

SDK:

// Get fields for specific issue type
fields, err := client.CreateMetaAPI.GetFields(ctx, "ABC", "10001")

# List fields for specific issue type in project
gojira fields --project ABC --issue-type 10001

docs.text: go-atlassian provides a Go SDK for interacting with the Jira REST API. The SDK is organized into packages with clear dependency boundaries.

docs.title: Package Structure

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"
)

func main() {
    // Create client with basic auth
    client, err := jira.NewClientFromBasicAuth(
        "https://your-instance.atlassian.net",
        "your-email@example.com",
        "your-api-token",
        false, // don't load custom fields on init
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Search issues
    issues, err := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssues("project = FOO AND status = Open", false)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Print results
    for _, issue := range issues {
        fmt.Printf("%s: %s\n", issue.Key, issue.Fields.Summary)
    }
}

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
The jira.Client is your entry point to the API. It provides access to service APIs:

  • client.IssueAPI - Issue operations (search, get, update)
  • client.CustomFieldAPI - Custom field operations (including duplicate name handling)
  • client.CreateMetaAPI - Project-based field discovery
  • client.BacklogAPI - Backlog operations

See Client for details.

docs.text:
Issues are returned as jira.Issues (a slice of jira.Issue). Use IssuesSet for advanced operations:

issuesSet, err := issues.IssuesSet(nil)

// Get counts by status
counts := issuesSet.CountsByStatus()

See Issues for details.

import "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian"

jql := jira.JQL{

    StatusesIncl: [][]string{{"Open", "In Progress"}},

query := jql.String()

Create a helper to read from environment:

import (
    "os"
    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"

        os.Getenv("JIRA_URL"),

client, err := jira.NewClientFromGoauthCLI(

docs.title: Client Structure
docs.text:
type Client struct {
    Config         *jira.Config
    HTTPClient     *http.Client
    JiraClient     *jira.Client
    Logger         *slog.Logger
    BacklogAPI     *BacklogService
    CreateMetaAPI  *CreateMetaService
    CustomFieldAPI *CustomFieldService
    IssueAPI       *IssueService
    CustomFieldSet *CustomFieldSet
}

docs.title: IssueAPI
docs.text:
The most commonly used service for issue operations:

// Search issues
issues, err := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssues("project = FOO", false)

// Get single issue
ctx := context.Background()
issue, err := client.IssueAPI.Issue(ctx, "FOO-123", nil)

// Get multiple issues
issues, err := client.IssueAPI.Issues(ctx, []string{"FOO-1", "FOO-2"}, nil)

// Update issue
resp, err := client.IssueAPI.IssuePatch(ctx, "FOO-123", patchBody)

docs.title: CustomFieldAPI
docs.text:
Access custom field definitions:

// Get all custom fields
fields, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFields()

// Get Epic Link field
epicField, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFieldEpicLink()

// Get field by exact ID
field, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFieldByID("customfield_10001")

// Get all fields matching a name (handles duplicates)
fields, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFieldsByName("Module")

// Get custom fields available in a specific project
ctx := context.Background()
projectFields, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFieldsForProject(ctx, "ABC")

docs.title: CreateMetaAPI
docs.text:
Discover which fields are available for issue creation in specific projects:

ctx := context.Background()

// Get issue types for a project
issueTypes, err := client.CreateMetaAPI.GetIssueTypes(ctx, "ABC")

// Get fields for a specific issue type
fields, err := client.CreateMetaAPI.GetFields(ctx, "ABC", "10001")

// Get all fields across all issue types in a project
allFields, err := client.CreateMetaAPI.GetAllFieldsForProject(ctx, "ABC")

docs.title: BacklogAPI
docs.text:
Backlog operations:

// Get backlog for a board
backlog, err := client.BacklogAPI.Backlog(boardID)

docs.title: Loading Custom Fields
docs.text:
Custom fields can be loaded during client initialization or later:

// Load during init
client, err := jira.NewClientFromBasicAuth(url, user, token, true)

// Or load later
err := client.LoadCustomFields()

// Access loaded fields
if client.CustomFieldSet != nil {
    name, err := client.CustomFieldSet.IDToName("customfield_10001")
}

docs.title: Handling Duplicate Custom Field Names
docs.text: Jira allows multiple custom fields to share the same display name (common when copying schemes or reinstalling apps). The SDK provides tools to handle this:

docs.title: Detecting Duplicates
docs.text:
fields, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFields()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Find which names appear more than once
duplicates := fields.DuplicateNames()
// Returns: ["Module", "Sprint"] (sorted)

// Map names to all their IDs
nameToIDs := fields.MapNameToIDs()
// Returns: {"Module": ["customfield_123", "customfield_456"], ...}

docs.title: Getting All Fields by Name
docs.text:
When a name might have duplicates, use GetCustomFieldsByName():

// Returns all fields named "Module" (may be multiple)
fields, err := client.CustomFieldAPI.GetCustomFieldsByName("Module")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

for _, f := range fields {
    fmt.Printf("ID: %s, Name: %s\n", f.ID, f.Name)
}

docs.title: Resolving Values from Issues
docs.text:
Use CustomFieldSet to extract values when field names are ambiguous:

// Load custom fields
err := client.LoadCustomFields()
cfSet := client.CustomFieldSet

// Get all values for fields named "Module" from an issue
values := cfSet.IssueCustomFieldsByName(issue, "Module")
for _, v := range values {
    fmt.Printf("Field %s (%s): %s\n", v.FieldName, v.FieldID, v.Value)
}

// Get only populated values (recommended for ambiguous names)
// The populated one is typically the active field
populated := cfSet.IssueCustomFieldsByNamePopulated(issue, "Module")
if len(populated) == 1 {
    fmt.Printf("Active Module field: %s\n", populated[0].Value)
}

docs.title: Counting by Custom Field Name
docs.text:
When aggregating issues, use name-based counting:

issuesSet, _ := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssuesSet("project = FOO")

// Count by field name, handling duplicates
counts, err := issuesSet.CountsByCustomFieldName("Module", cfSet, true)
// true = only count issues with populated values

serverURL := client.Config.ServerURL

// Modify config

Set a logger for debug output:

import "log/slog"

For operations not covered by service APIs, access the underlying clients:

// Raw HTTP client

docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"
)

func main() {
    // Create client
    client, err := jira.NewClientFromBasicAuth(
        "https://your-instance.atlassian.net",
        "your-email@example.com",
        "your-api-token",
        true, // Load custom fields
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Search issues
    issues, err := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssues("project = FOO AND status = Open", false)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    fmt.Printf("Found %d issues\n", len(issues))

        if err != nil {
            log.Fatal(err)
        }
        fmt.Printf("Issue: %s - %s\n", issue.Key, issue.Fields.Summary)
    }
}

docs.title: Issues
docs.text: The SDK provides several types for working with Jira issues.

docs.title: jira.Issues
docs.text:
A slice of jira.Issue from the go-jira library:

issues, err := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssues("project = FOO", false)
// issues is jira.Issues ([]jira.Issue)

for _, issue := range issues {
    fmt.Printf("%s: %s\n", issue.Key, issue.Fields.Summary)

docs.title: jira.IssueMore
docs.text:
A wrapper around jira.Issue with convenience methods:

import "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"

issue := issues[0]

// Convenience accessors
key := im.Key()
summary := im.Summary()

typeName := im.TypeName()

docs.title: jira.IssuesSet
docs.text:

// Create from Issues
issuesSet, err := issues.IssuesSet(nil)
if err != nil {

// Get counts
countsByStatus := issuesSet.CountsByStatus()
countsByType := issuesSet.CountsByType(true, true)
countsByProject := issuesSet.CountsByProject()

filtered := issuesSet.FilterByStatus("Open")

issue := issues[0]

package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"

func main() {

docs.title: JQL Builder
docs.text: The root package provides a JQL builder for constructing Jira Query Language queries programmatically.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
import "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian"

jql := jira.JQL{
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO"}},
    StatusesIncl: [][]string{{"Open", "In Progress"}},
}

query := jql.String()
// Result: "project = 'FOO' AND status IN ('Open', 'In Progress')"

docs.title: JQL Structure
docs.text:
The JQL struct supports include and exclude conditions for various fields:

type JQL struct {
    // Date conditions
    CreatedGT       *time.Time
    CreatedGTE      *time.Time
    CreatedLT       *time.Time
    CreatedLTE      *time.Time
    DueGT           *time.Time
    DueGTE          *time.Time
    DueLT           *time.Time
    DueLTE          *time.Time
    UpdatedGT       *time.Time
    UpdatedGTE      *time.Time
    UpdatedLT       *time.Time
    UpdatedLTE      *time.Time

    // String field conditions (outer = AND, inner = IN)
    FiltersIncl     [][]string
    FiltersExcl     [][]string
    IssuesIncl      [][]string
    IssuesExcl      [][]string
    KeysIncl        [][]string
    KeysExcl        [][]string
    LabelsIncl      [][]string
    LabelsExcl      [][]string
    ParentsIncl     [][]string
    ParentsExcl     [][]string
    ProjectsIncl    [][]string
    ProjectsExcl    [][]string
    ResolutionIncl  [][]string
    ResolutionExcl  [][]string
    StatusesIncl    [][]string
    StatusesExcl    [][]string
    TypesIncl       [][]string
    TypesExcl       [][]string

    // Text search
    SummaryLike     []string
    SummaryNotLike  []string
    TextLike        []string
    TextNotLike     []string

    // Custom fields
    CustomFieldIncl map[string][]string
    CustomFieldExcl map[string][]string

    // Raw JQL fragments
    Raw             []string
}

docs.title: Single Project, Single Status
docs.text:
jql := jira.JQL{
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO"}},
    StatusesIncl: [][]string{{"Open"}},
}
// project = 'FOO' AND status = 'Open'

docs.title: Multiple Projects
docs.text:
jql := jira.JQL{
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO", "BAR", "BAZ"}},
}
// project IN ('FOO', 'BAR', 'BAZ')

docs.title: Multiple Status Groups (AND)
docs.text:
jql := jira.JQL{
    StatusesIncl: [][]string{
        {"Open", "In Progress"},  // First condition
        {"Blocked"},               // AND this condition
    },
}
// status IN ('Open', 'In Progress') AND status = 'Blocked'

docs.title: Exclude Conditions
docs.text:
jql := jira.JQL{
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO"}},
    StatusesExcl: [][]string{{"Done", "Closed"}},
}
// project = 'FOO' AND status NOT IN ('Done', 'Closed')

docs.title: Date Filtering
docs.text:
import "time"

sevenDaysAgo := time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, -7)
jql := jira.JQL{
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO"}},
    CreatedGTE:   &sevenDaysAgo,
}
// project = 'FOO' AND createdDate >= 2024-01-08

docs.title: Text Search
docs.text:
jql := jira.JQL{
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO"}},
    TextLike:     []string{"error"},
}
// project = 'FOO' AND text ~ "error"

docs.title: Summary Search
docs.text:
jql := jira.JQL{
    SummaryLike: []string{"login", "authentication"},
}
// summary ~ "login" AND summary ~ "authentication"

docs.title: Custom Fields
docs.text:
jql := jira.JQL{
    CustomFieldIncl: map[string][]string{
        "customfield_10001": {"Team A", "Team B"},
    },
}
// cf[10001] IN ('Team A', 'Team B')

docs.title: Raw JQL
docs.text:
For complex conditions not supported by the builder:

jql := jira.JQL{
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO"}},
    Raw: []string{
        "fixVersion = '1.0'",
        "sprint in openSprints()",
    },
}
// project = 'FOO' AND fixVersion = '1.0' AND sprint in openSprints()

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
jql := jira.JQL{
    LabelsIncl: [][]string{{"bug", "urgent"}},
}
// labels IN ('bug', 'urgent')

docs.title: Query String
docs.text:
Generate URL-encoded query string:

jql := jira.JQL{
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO"}},
}

qs := jql.QueryString()
// jql=project%20%3D%20%27FOO%27

docs.title: JQL Metadata
docs.text:
Store query metadata for tracking:

jql := jira.JQL{
    Meta: jira.JQLMeta{
        Name:        "Open Bugs",
        Description: "All open bugs in FOO project",
        QueryTime:   time.Now(),
    },
    ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO"}},
    TypesIncl:    [][]string{{"Bug"}},
    StatusesIncl: [][]string{{"Open"}},
}

docs.title: Splitting Long Queries
docs.text:
For very long value lists that exceed Jira's limits:

values := []string{"KEY-1", "KEY-2", ..., "KEY-1000"}

jqls := jira.JQLStringsSimple(
    "key",    // Field name
    false,    // Exclude (false = include)
    values,   // Values
    0,        // Max length (0 = default)
)

// Returns multiple JQL strings, each under the length limit
for _, jql := range jqls {
    issues, _ := client.IssueAPI.SearchIssues(jql, false)
    // Process issues...
}

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "time"

    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian"
    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"
)

func main() {
    // Build JQL query
    oneMonthAgo := time.Now().AddDate(0, -1, 0)

    jql := jira.JQL{
        ProjectsIncl: [][]string{{"FOO", "BAR"}},
        TypesIncl:    [][]string{{"Bug", "Task"}},
        StatusesExcl: [][]string{{"Done", "Closed"}},
        CreatedGTE:   &oneMonthAgo,
    }

    query := jql.String()
    fmt.Printf("JQL: %s\n", query)

    // Use with client
    client, err := jira.NewClientFromBasicAuth(
        "https://your-instance.atlassian.net",
        "your-email@example.com",
        "your-api-token",
        false,
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: Integrate go-atlassian with Dashforge to provide a powerful, reusable report generation system that supports both interactive notebook-style exploration and static report export. This integration enables users to create Jira-based reports and dashboards using a JSON-first intermediate representation (IR) that can be rendered interactively or exported to static formats.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
Currently, go-atlassian provides excellent CLI and SDK capabilities for querying Jira data and generating reports (velocity, burndown, worklog, cycle-time). However:

  1. No unified report format - Each report command outputs independently with no way to combine them
  2. Limited visualization - Output is text-based (JSON, table, CSV, markdown)
  3. No interactivity - Reports are static snapshots with no drill-down or filtering
  4. No reusability - Report definitions cannot be saved, shared, or version-controlled

docs.title: Solution Overview
docs.text:
Create a hybrid integration where:

  • go-atlassian handles Jira data fetching, transformation, and business logic
  • Dashforge provides the visualization IR, rendering, and export capabilities

This produces a Jira Report IR that transforms into Dashforge Dashboard IR for rendering.

// Variable represents a configurable parameter in a report.

// report/engine.go

package report

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/grokify/go-atlassian/jira"
)

// Engine executes report definitions and produces Dashforge IR.
type Engine struct {
    client     *jira.Client
    cache      *Cache
    processors map[SectionType]SectionProcessor
}

// NewEngine creates a new report engine.
func NewEngine(client *jira.Client) *Engine {
    e := &Engine{
        client:     client,
        cache:      NewCache(),
        processors: make(map[SectionType]SectionProcessor),
    }

    // Register built-in processors
    e.RegisterProcessor(SectionTypeMarkdown, &MarkdownProcessor{})
    e.RegisterProcessor(SectionTypeJQL, &JQLProcessor{client: client})
    e.RegisterProcessor(SectionTypeVelocity, &VelocityProcessor{client: client})
    e.RegisterProcessor(SectionTypeBurndown, &BurndownProcessor{client: client})
    e.RegisterProcessor(SectionTypeWorklog, &WorklogProcessor{client: client})
    e.RegisterProcessor(SectionTypeCycleTime, &CycleTimeProcessor{client: client})
    e.RegisterProcessor(SectionTypeMetric, &MetricProcessor{client: client})

    return e
}

// RegisterProcessor registers a custom section processor.
func (e *Engine) RegisterProcessor(sectionType SectionType, processor SectionProcessor) {
    e.processors[sectionType] = processor
}

// Execute runs the report and returns a Dashforge Dashboard IR.
func (e *Engine) Execute(ctx context.Context, def *Definition, vars map[string]any) (*DashboardIR, error) {
    // Resolve variables
    resolvedVars := e.resolveVariables(def.Variables, vars)

    // Create execution context
    execCtx := &ExecutionContext{
        Context:   ctx,
        Variables: resolvedVars,
        Cache:     e.cache,
    }

    // Process sections
    widgets := make([]WidgetIR, 0, len(def.Sections))
    dataSources := make([]DataSourceIR, 0)

    for i, section := range def.Sections {
        processor, ok := e.processors[section.Type]
        if !ok {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown section type: %s", section.Type)
        }

        result, err := processor.Process(execCtx, &section)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("process section %s: %w", section.ID, err)
        }

        // Add data source
        if result.DataSource != nil {
            dataSources = append(dataSources, *result.DataSource)
        }

        // Add widget with auto-positioning if not specified
        widget := result.Widget
        if widget.Position == nil {
            widget.Position = &PositionIR{
                X: 0,
                Y: i * 4, // Stack vertically
                W: 12,
                H: 4,
            }
        }
        widgets = append(widgets, widget)
    }

    // Build dashboard IR
    dashboard := &DashboardIR{
        ID:          def.ID,
        Title:       def.Title,
        Description: def.Description,
        Version:     def.Version,
        Layout:      LayoutIR{Columns: 12},
        DataSources: dataSources,
        Widgets:     widgets,
        Theme:       e.convertTheme(def.Theme),
    }

    return dashboard, nil
}

// SectionProcessor processes a section and produces widget IR.
type SectionProcessor interface {
    Process(ctx *ExecutionContext, section *Section) (*SectionResult, error)
}

// ExecutionContext provides context for section processing.
type ExecutionContext struct {
    Context   context.Context
    Variables map[string]any
    Cache     *Cache
}

// SectionResult contains the output of processing a section.
type SectionResult struct {
    Widget     WidgetIR
    DataSource *DataSourceIR
}

        Embedded:  true,
    }
    return e.template.Execute(w, data)
}

docs.title: 2. Missing Interfaces
docs.text:
Current state: No interfaces defined in any package.

Recommended interfaces (P2 - post v1):

// rest/interfaces.go

// IssueGetter defines issue retrieval operations.
type IssueGetter interface {
    Issue(ctx context.Context, key string, opts *GetQueryOptions) (*jira.Issue, error)
    Issues(ctx context.Context, keys []string, opts *GetQueryOptions) (Issues, error)
}

// IssueSearcher defines issue search operations.
type IssueSearcher interface {
    SearchIssues(jql string, retrieveAll bool) (Issues, error)
    SearchIssuesPages(jql string, startAt, maxResults, maxPages int) (Issues, error)
}

// CommentGetter defines comment retrieval operations.
type CommentGetter interface {
    GetComments(ctx context.Context, issueKey string, maxResults int) (*CommentsResponse, error)
}

Benefits:

  • Enables unit testing with mocks
  • Supports dependency injection
  • Documents expected behavior
